cards.def: Hygelac rewarded Beowulf with seven thousand hides of land, a hall, and a throne.
Beowulf gave Hygelac four matching bay horses along with Heorogar's war-gear.
Beowulf gave Queen Hygd three saddled horses and the torque that Wealhtheow had given him.
Beowulf escaped the Friesland raid by swimming home carrying thirty sets of armor he had won.
Hygelac's raid on the Frisians, recorded by the historian Gregory of Tours, took place around 521, which dates the poem's events to the 500s.
Beowulf was fostered at King Hrethel's court from the age of seven.
Hrethel had three sons, Herebeald, Haethcyn, and Hygelac.
Beowulf ruled the Geats for fifty winters before the dragon woke.
The dragon had guarded its hoard for three hundred years before the thief stole the cup.
The treasure had lain underground for a thousand winters, according to the scene after the dragon's death.
Beowulf went to the barrow with eleven companions and the thief as a forced guide, making thirteen.
The dragon attacked three times, and on the third attack it sank its fangs into Beowulf's neck.
The dead dragon measured fifty feet from head to tail.
Ten warriors fled into the wood and came back only after the dragon and Beowulf were dead.
Wiglaf chose seven of the best thanes and entered the barrow as the eighth to bring out the treasure.
The Geats took ten days to build Beowulf's barrow on the headland.
Twelve warriors rode around the barrow chanting dirges in praise of Beowulf.
